en.title: Matthew Perry Docuseries and Spooky K-Drama Headline Netflix's Halloween Week
en.summary: Netflix is dropping a heartfelt tribute to Matthew Perry and a chilling K-drama just in time for Halloween. Get ready for a week of emotional journeys and spine-tingling scares.
en.body:
As Halloween weekend descends, Netflix is pulling out all the stops to keep subscribers glued to their screens. This coming week, from October 26th to November 1st, 2026, the streamer is poised to deliver a slate of new Originals that promises to tug at heartstrings and send shivers down spines alike.

Leading the charge is **The One About Matthew Perry**, a docuseries premiering Tuesday that serves as a loving tribute to the beloved actor three years after his untimely passing. The series delves into Perry's extraordinary life and career, charting his meteoric rise to fame as the unforgettable Chandler Bing on **Friends** through his candid struggles with addiction and the lasting legacy he leaves behind. For the legions of **Friends** fans worldwide, this promises to be an essential, emotionally charged watch, blending laughter and tears in equal measure.

## Spooky K-Drama and Live Darts Hijinks

Just in time for the spooky season, **Dead-End Job** arrives on Friday. This eight-episode limited series is a horror-comedy K-drama starring **Alchemy of Souls**' **Lee Jae Wook** as Hyuk-jun. He plays a young man who believes he's landed the part-time gig of a lifetime, earning an astronomical hourly wage through a mysterious entity known as the Spyder Human Resource Center. However, what begins as a dream quickly devolves into a living nightmare, with co-stars **Go Min Si**, **Kim Min Ha**, and **Lee Hee Joon** rounding out the ensemble. The blend of horror and comedy, coupled with a high-concept premise, positions this as a must-watch for K-drama aficionados looking for something fresh and thrilling.

Beyond these narrative highlights, the week also includes **Beat Luke Littler**, a live event where the world number one darts player puts his title on the line, offering a dose of real-time sporting drama. The streamer is also bolstering its library significantly on Sunday, November 1st, with over 35 licensed titles set to drop, including fan-favorite films like **Bridesmaids**, **Whiplash**, **Stand by Me**, and **The Mummy**.

## A Packed November Launch

The anticipation is palpable for the transition into November, with Netflix clearly aiming to capture audience attention with a diverse range of content. The influx of licensed titles on the first day of the month alone demonstrates a strategy to offer something for everyone, from acclaimed dramas to beloved comedies and action-packed adventures. The week's original offerings, however, showcase Netflix's commitment to powerful storytelling, whether it's celebrating the life of a television icon or diving headfirst into genre thrills. The platform is clearly banking on emotional documentaries and genre-bending K-dramas to hook viewers as the year winds down.

## What's Next

With **The One About Matthew Perry** arriving Tuesday and **Dead-End Job** premiering Friday, the week is packed with compelling new Originals. Sunday's massive influx of over 35 licensed films and series, including **Bridesmaids** and **Whiplash**, sets the stage for a robust November content rollout.

For the full list of November 2026 releases , keep it locked here on What’s on Netflix. Best New Shows and Movies Coming to Netflix This Week The One About Matthew Perry (Season 1) Coming to Netflix: Tuesday Three years on from his passing, Netflix pays tribute to one of the most beloved sitcom stars of all time. This docuseries looks back at Matthew Perry’s life and career, from becoming a household name as Chandler Bing on Friends to his candid public battles with addiction and the legacy he left behind. Expect plenty of laughs alongside the tears. For Friends fans, this is the must-watch of the week. Dead-End Job (Limited Series) Coming to Netflix: Friday Just in time for Halloween, Alchemy of Souls star Lee Jae Wook leads this eight-episode horror-comedy K-drama. He plays Hyuk-jun, a young man who lands a seemingly perfect part-time gig paying 50 times the usual hourly wage through a mysterious agency called Spyder Human Resource Center. Naturally, the dream job quickly turns into a nightmare. Go Min Si, Kim Min Ha and Lee Hee Joon co-star. We’ve made big statements about K-dramas being the next Squid Game before and they’ve never come to fruition so we’ll set expectations low. That said, this looks from the outside super interesting and some definite crossovers.  The Fall of El Mayo (Limited Series) Coming to Netflix: Thursday In July 2024, Sinaloa Cartel co-founder Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada landed at a small New Mexico airport alongside El Chapo’s son and was taken into US custody. Was it a kidnapping, a betrayal, or a covert operation? Directed by Peabody and Emmy winner Darren Foster and Miguel Fernández Flores, this three-part docuseries digs into exclusive testimony, unseen archive footage and hundreds of court records to unpack one of organized crime’s most mysterious downfalls.
